methodology.study_design: Deliberative consensus process combining crowdsourcing, literature reviews, online discussions, and two in-person workshops over two years to identify priority research questions
methodology.sample_description: Historical ecology researchers and practitioners from anthropology, archaeology, and related disciplines; 47 workshop participants in Vancouver second-stage meeting
methodology.sector: academic research in anthropology, archaeology, and historical ecology
methodology.technology_context: historical ecology, human-environment interactions, environmental resource management and policy; no AI, LLM, or conversational systems

eligibility.exclusion_reason: The article identifies priority research questions for historical ecology in anthropology and archaeology. It does not address LLMs, generative AI, conversational systems, or governance of AI in regulated environments.
eligibility.decision_rationale: Python triage matched generic terms such as governance, ethics, education, and policy in an environmental-historical context, but the full text contains no LLM, chatbot, agent, RAG, guardrails, observability, or AI accountability content. Governance references concern resource and environmental management, conservation, and Indigenous land governance, which are outside the review scope.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Topic mismatch is unambiguous from title, abstract, and full-text excerpts; no AI or conversational technology content present.

appraisal.notes: Methodologically sound consensus exercise for historical ecology agenda-setting, but not transferable to conversational AI governance in regulated LLM systems. Ethics approval reported; limitations of consensus process not deeply discussed in provided excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Internally coherent for historical ecology research prioritization, but relevance to LLM conversational governance is negligible despite incidental keyword overlap on governance and policy.

coding.subtheme: Resource management and environmental governance questions

synthesis.main_claim: A consensus-driven process produced 50 priority research questions for historical ecology from anthropological and archaeological perspectives, organized into six interrelated themes.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a structured research agenda for historical ecology spanning climate change, biodiversity, methods, communication, and resource/environmental management and governance.
synthesis.use_in_review: Exclude from evidence synthesis. Not usable as central, supporting, or foundational evidence for conversational governance of LLMs in regulated settings; keyword overlap on governance and ethics is contextual and environmental, not AI-related.

evidence.claim: Six thematic nodes structure the 50 questions
evidence.excerpt: Six interrelated themes arose from our consensus-building workshop model: (1) climate and environmental change and variability; (2) multi-scalar, multi-disciplinary; (3) biodiversity and community ecology; (4) resource and environmental management and governance; (5) methods and applications; and (6) communication
